problem: Which of the following lines is perpendicular to $x+3y=6?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following lines is perpendicular to $8x-y=2?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For the two lines to be perpendicular, their slopes must multiply to $-1.$

To find the slope of the given line $8x-y=2,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}8x-y & =2 \\ -y & =-8x+2 \\ y & =8x-2\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope of the given line is $8.$

Looking at the answer choices, the line $y=-\frac{1}{8}x+8$ has a slope of $-\frac{1}{8}.$

Multiplying the slopes together, we have

$$
8\cdot (-\frac{1}{8})=-1.
$$

Since the slopes multiply to $-1,$ we conclude that the line $y=-\frac{1}{8}x+8$ is perpendicular to the given line.
